title: The one division the crypt never makes

objectives.statement: Trace one chromosome pair through both meiotic divisions, naming which physical connection is undone at each division and what each product contains, contrast that with what a single mitotic division separates, and state how many functional gametes one meiosis yields in spermatogenesis and in oogenesis.

Compute the number of whole-chromosome combinations independent assortment alone can produce in one person's gametes and in the zygotes of a couple, compute crossovers per chromosome pair from measured genome-wide crossover totals, and state the assumption that any larger estimate of gamete diversity depends on.

Predict the products of a meiosis in which one chromosome pair fails to separate at division I versus at division II, state how many of the four products carry an abnormal chromosome number in each case and what the abnormal product contains, and apply centromere-marker reasoning to infer which division failed.

Separate the documented association between maternal age and aneuploidy from the mechanisms proposed to explain it, state for a cited study what its design can and cannot establish about mechanism, and identify statements that go further than the cited evidence supports.

Explain why a continuously renewing somatic tissue such as the colonic crypt runs no meiosis, using the difference between what a mitotic and a meiotic division separate, and contrast the role that new chromosome combinations play in the germ line with the role that new genetic differences play in a crypt.

scenes.title: A tissue that divides for a lifetime and never does this
One replication, two divisions, and the reason there are two
Count it: how many different gametes can one person make?
Four products, and the meiosis that keeps only one
Which division failed, and how anyone could tell
A well-documented effect with an unfinished explanation
Practice: trace it, count it, then say what failed
Clinical wrap-up: in a crypt, a new combination is the other kind of problem
